dialog.body: Public Works, this is Lorraine, how can I help you this afternoon?

Hi, yes, Lorraine. My name is Siobhan McCarthy, I'm at 12 Brewer Street, up in the Fifth Ward, and I'm calling about that drain at the corner. Again. Because apparently once wasn't enough, and twice wasn't enough either.
Okay, Siobhan. 12 Brewer Street. And this is the storm drain at the corner?

The corner, yes. The catch basin, whatever you call it. So I called Sunday, right after the nor'easter, Saturday into Sunday, the whole street was up to the curb. And the young man on the phone was very nice, he said a crew would come Monday. And they did come, I'll give them that. I watched them out the front window. Two fellas, they swept the leaves off the top of the grate, stood there maybe ten minutes, and drove off. That's it. That was the whole repair.
So a crew came out yesterday, Monday, and cleared the grate on top.

The top. Just the top. And it's Tuesday afternoon and I still have water sitting there. Now, my tenant, Judith, she rents the in-law unit over the garage, she called you people back in January about the same exact thing, and they came out then too and did the same exact thing, swept the top. So you see where I'm going with this.
I do. Actually, I think I may have taken that call from your address last month. Gardiner?

That's her, yes. Judith. Lovely girl. She drives the school bus, so she's up at some ungodly hour, and she said she had to wade out to the car that morning. Anyway. [line breaks up] ...the yard is just soaked, Lorraine. Squishy. You step on the grass and it goes right over your shoe. And there's water standing right up against the foundation on the street side.
I'm sorry, you broke up there for a second. Water standing against the foundation. Is any of it getting into the house?

No, no, the basement's dry, thank God, I checked it twice. House didn't take a drop. But it's sitting right there against the wall like it's waiting for an invitation, and I don't love that. The whole block drains down toward that corner, see, everything runs downhill to that one grate, and that grate looks plugged to me. Not the leaves on top. Underneath. Something's in there.
Okay. So the whole block drains toward the corner, the grate looks plugged below the surface, and you've got standing water in the yard against the foundation, but the house and basement stayed dry.

That's it exactly. And you know what, I was on the laptop this morning trying to look up who even owns that drain, and I look down and the little camera on top, the webcam, I'd forgotten to put the sticker back over it. My husband's always on me about that. Sitting there in my bathrobe, staring at the thing like it was staring at me. Anyway, I couldn't find the answer. Is that drain the city's or the state's? Because if it's the state I'll call the state and stop bothering you.
Brewer Street's a city street, so that catch basin would be ours. You're in the right place.
Well. Good. Then somebody from the city needs to look inside the thing instead of sweeping it like a front porch.

I hear you. What I'm going to do is put this in as a catch basin backup, and I'm going to note that the grate's been cleared twice, February second and yesterday, and the water's still not going down, so it's likely blocked below. I've got a crew scheduled to come out tomorrow, Wednesday.
Tomorrow. [inaudible] ...and will they actually open it this time?
Sorry, you cut out. Did you ask if they'll open it?
Yes. Will they open it up, or am I going to watch two more fellas with a broom?
I'm writing it right in the notes that the surface has already been cleared twice and the resident believes it's plugged underneath. That's what they'll see when they pull the order.
Fine. Put 'resident' in capital letters.
I'll put it in strong. Can I get a good number for you in case they need to reach you?
It's my cell, 401-555-0127. It's terrible reception in this kitchen, so if it goes to voicemail, don't be offended.
401-555-0127. And that's 12 Brewer Street, crew tomorrow, Wednesday, for the corner catch basin.
Wednesday. Alright. Third time's the charm, they say. I'll be at the window.
If it's still backing up after they come, call us back and reference today's call. Have a good rest of your afternoon, Siobhan.
We'll see. Thank you, Lorraine.
